note: 52a Kofo Abayomi St. Sundowners that roll into the night. Best for groups who want one venue.

name: Truth Beach Club
tagline: Beach club, harder edge
note: Pool, seafood, and Sunday parties that run from noon till late. Ladies' day Sundays.

name: Landmark Beach
tagline: Demolished for the Lagos–Calabar coastal highway
note: Landmark Beach was demolished in April 2024 to make way for the Lagos–Calabar coastal highway. The resort — six years old, with beach clubs, cabanas and water sports — was cleared in a week; the federal government said the land was on its right-of-way. There is no beach access at the old site. Do not travel here expecting a beach day.
address: Water Corporation Drive, Oniru, Lagos
closedNote: Landmark Beach was demolished in April 2024 for the Lagos–Calabar coastal highway. Its Google listing at Water Corporation Drive, Oniru is marked permanently closed, and there is no beach access at the site. The Landmark Africa Group is rebuilding elsewhere; this entry is kept so you do not turn up expecting a beach day.

name: Elegushi Royal Beach
tagline: The loud one
note: Gate ₦1,000–2,000. Independent lounges (Wave, 234 Loft, Skyfall) charge ₦2,000–3,000 more; cabanas up to ₦150k. Jet skis, horses, speakers.
address: Lekki-Epe Expressway, Ikate, Lekki, Lagos

name: Tarkwa Bay
tagline: A boat-only beach with calm water and city views
note: Tarkwa Bay is a sheltered artificial beach just off the Lagos harbour — calmer water than the open Atlantic beaches, which is why people swim here and take surf lessons. It's an island, so the only way in is by boat: 15–30 minutes from the CMS, Falomo or Victoria Island jetties. Day entry is about ₦2,000, with chairs and a thatched tent from around ₦500 for the day. On the water you can swim, book surf lessons, hire a jet ski, and eat grilled fish from the shore. There's a small resident community and a jetty station. Sort your return boat before you settle in — the last boats back matter more than the first ones out. Overnight stays aren't really a thing here; this is a day-beach, not a campsite.
address: Tarkwa Bay Island, Lagos Harbour (boat from Falomo or the CMS jetty)

name: Oniru Private Beach
tagline: Closest proper beach to VI
note: Behind the Oniru royal estate, off Admiralty Way. Quieter midweek, busy on Sundays.
address: 1 Ligali Ayorinde Street, Oniru, Victoria Island, Lagos

name: La Campagne Tropicana
tagline: The resort escape
note: An hour-plus out on Lekki-Epe. ₦10,000 entry, thatched stays from around ₦70,000. Go for a night, not an afternoon.
address: Ikegun, Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos (off the Lekki-Epe Expressway)

name: Terra Kulture
tagline: Nigerian food, theatre and a 400-seat arena
note: A restaurant, art gallery and theatre in one compound. The Arena is a 400-seat performance hall for live shows, theatre, music and cultural events. The kitchen serves Nigerian food Monday to Sunday, 9am–10pm, though it closes before the venue does; book at restaurant.terrakulture.com or +234 810 422 4137.
address: 1376 Tiamiyu Savage St, Victoria Island, Lagos

tagline: The slow brunch
note: Nobs & Berries sits on Adebisi Ogunniyi Crescent in Ikoyi, but Google currently lists it as temporarily closed while delivery apps still show it open — call before you travel.

address: 1637 Adetokunbo Ademola St, Victoria Island, Lagos

note: 7 Adeboro St, Itamaga. Slides, VR, cinema and a grill under one roof — worth it if you are that side.

tagline: Africa's longest canopy walk
note: 200-acre reserve. Go early, take the canopy walk, keep your phone in a pocket with a zip.
address: Lekki-Epe Expressway, Lekki, Lagos

name: Freedom Park

note: 1 Broad St. Jazz, spoken word, theatre and a bar. The cheapest good night out on the Island.

name: New Afrika Shrine
tagline: Fela's house, still playing
note: Open-air hall, hot and loud, beer cheap. Femi Kuti's Sunday Jump starts around 7.30pm; Seun and Egypt 80 usually take Thursday. Most nights free; headline nights ₦2,000–5,000.
address: 1 NERDC Road, Agidingbi, Ikeja

name: Ozone Cinemas

note: Six screens inside E-Centre, with an arcade and shops below. Cheaper than the Island and full of students midweek. Book online and skip the box office.
address: E-Centre, 1–11 Commercial Avenue, Sabo, Yaba

name: Purple Maryland
tagline: Mall, rink and cinema

name: Bukka Hut
tagline: Amala without the guesswork
note: A cleaned-up buka chain: amala with ewedu and gbegiri, egusi, ofada and ram suya rice. Mains ₦4,000–6,500, breakfast from about ₦2,000. Tables turn fast.
address: 271 Herbert Macaulay Way, Alagomeji, Yaba

name: Ilashe Beach
tagline: Boat-only island beach
note: Boat only: there is no road access, so you have to rent or book a boat — 20–40 minutes from Falomo or the Elegushi jetty. Shared boats about ₦5,000 return, speedboats from ₦50,000. No gate fee, quiet sand, grilled fish on the shore. Fix your return boat first.
address: Ilashe Island (boat from Falomo or the Elegushi jetty)

name: National Museum Lagos
tagline: The national collection, on the Onikan roundabout
note: Founded in 1957, the National Museum holds the country's flagship collection: Nok terracotta, Ife and Benin bronzes, Igbo-Ukwu copper work and ethnographic exhibits from across Nigeria. An hour here gives the city's history a shape.
address: Onikan, Lagos Island, Lagos

name: Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge
tagline: The cable-stayed bridge everyone stops to photograph
note: Commissioned in May 2013, the 1.36 km bridge is Nigeria's first cable-stayed crossing, its single pylon throwing cables over Five Cowries Creek between Ikoyi and Lekki. See it from the Ikoyi end at sunset, when the lagoon goes copper — the best city view that costs nothing.
address: Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge, Lagos

name: Jaekel House
tagline: An 1898 railway mansion with a garden and a story
note: Built in 1898 as the residence of the Nigerian Railway Corporation's general manager, Jaekel House is a timber-and-verandah mansion in Ebute Metta, restored in 2010 and named after a long-serving NRC superintendent. Inside is a small museum: railway photographs from the 1940s to the 1970s, tools and equipment. Outside, old trees and a garden that makes the traffic feel far away.
address: 17 Federal Road, Ebute Metta, Lagos

name: Tafawa Balewa Square
tagline: The square where independence was celebrated
note: This is the old Lagos Race Course, where Nigeria's independence ceremony was held on 1 October 1960. The square itself was built in 1972 and named after the first prime minister; the stands, the Remembrance Arcade and Independence House are all still there. Come for the scale and the colonial-era city around it.
address: Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos Island, Lagos

name: National Theatre
tagline: The concrete shell on the Lagos lagoon
note: Completed in 1976 for FESTAC '77, the National Theatre's stacked concrete form is the city's most recognisable silhouette. A Bankers' Committee restoration reopened it on 1 October 2025 as the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts. Check what is on before you go; even from outside it is worth the detour at dusk.
address: National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos

name: Cathedral Church of Christ
tagline: Gothic Revival on Marina, founded in 1869
note: The cathedral was founded on this Marina site in 1869, though the present Gothic Revival building — clock tower, stained glass and pipe organ — dates from 1924 to 1946. Weekday tours run from 10am to 4pm; outside them the churchyard is one of the quietest corners of Lagos Island.
address: 29 Marina, Lagos Island, Lagos

Google Maps lists the resort on Okun Ajah road, Mopo Akinlade Rd, Ajah, Lagos 106104, with a phone number and resort-site reviews. address: Okun Ajah road, Mopo Akinlade Rd, Ajah, Lagos

It is an attraction for photographs rather than a long visit, and it is ticketed separately from Landmark Beach next door, so buy the house ticket on its own and go early or off-peak to get the rooms without a queue.
